facts.activity_file: providing and briefing a fire watch

consequence.label: first aid or minor property damage

authorisation of hot work adjacent to live plant

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: injury during a planned shutdown on K-7301

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage.

defences.finding: Control GAS_TEST_BEFORE_AND_DURING_HOT_WORK: the atmospheric gas testing before and during hot work had been bypassed, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an individual or team action.
Control HOT_WORK_AUTHORISATION: the authorisation of hot work adjacent to live plant had been bypassed, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the authorisation of hot work adjacent to live plant on K-7301, M-7301 and PT-7301 and record the critical control verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip on K-7301, M-7301 and PT-7301 and record the critical control verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in authorising hot work, specifically providing and briefing a fire watch. K-7301 (vapour recovery compressor) is in service for loading vapour recovery. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the atmospheric gas testing before and during hot work had been bypassed. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 25 February 2018 an incident occurred on K-7301, M-7301 and PT-7301 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a planned shutdown, releasing chemical energy held as hydrocarbon.
